missed_day: You were absent yesterday. Don't explain. Sit.
A lapse. Note it, then drop it. Regret is wasted focus.
The mind wanders. Bring it back. Same with the day.
Yesterday is not my concern. Today is.
You broke the pattern. Start a new one. Now.
I waited. You did not come. I'm still waiting.
Missing once is nothing. Getting comfortable with it is everything.
You lost a day. Don't lose another looking for it.
Distraction won yesterday. It does not win twice.
Discipline is a promise to yourself. You broke one. Keep the next.
No training. No progress. Simple arithmetic.
I don't need you to feel bad. I need you to sit down and focus.
Hmph. Yesterday you let the noise win.
comeback: Hmph. So you can be taught.
Coming back is harder than starting. I noticed.
No ceremony. You're here. That is enough.
The lapse is over. Don't carry it into the session.
You sat down without being told. Progress.
A mind that returns is a trained mind. That is all training is.
You're here. Focus. That's all I ask.
Good. The gap is closed. Don't open it again.
I won't mention yesterday. You'll remember it anyway.
Returning is a skill. You have it. Need it less.
Hmph. You came back without being dragged. Noted.
Discipline lost, discipline regained. Now hold it.
Your focus wandered off. It found its way home. Good.
streak_milestone: {streak} days unbroken. You're becoming difficult to distract.
{streak} days. The weight is the same. You are not.
Hmph. {streak}. Don't let it make you careless.
{streak} days of quiet work. Few manage ten.
{streak}. I expected less of you. I was wrong.
A {streak}-day streak. Don't look at me. Keep going.
{streak} days. The mind sharpens with use.
{streak}. You're quieter now. That is strength.
{streak} days of focus. Don't speak of it. Continue.
{streak} in a row. You're no longer fighting yourself.
{streak} days. Don't admire the number. Admire nothing. Work.
boss_defeated: You stayed patient against {boss}. That won it.
Hmph. {boss} underestimated you. I no longer do.
Done. Don't celebrate long. There's always another.
You saw where {boss} was weak and kept at it. Good eyes.
{boss} fell to discipline, not luck. Remember which.
A long fight, well held. I have nothing to correct.
Good. Now rest your mind. It did most of the fighting.
{boss} lost to your patience. Most do.
Hmph. {boss} is defeated. Your focus never broke.
You were calm against {boss}. Calm wins wars.
{boss} is beaten. Now meditate. Victory clouds the mind.
Well done. {boss} never understood what consistency can do.
A clean finish against {boss}. I watched all of it.
Hmph. I expected {boss} to last longer. You've grown.
idle: One task. All of your attention. Nothing else exists.
The noise in your head is not an order. Ignore it.
Don't wait to feel ready. Ready comes after you begin.
Your enemy today is the urge to check something else.
Clear the mind. Then fill it with one thing.
Focus is a muscle. Train it.
A quiet hour is worth more than a busy day.
Your attention is your strength. Don't spend it cheaply.
Everything else can wait. It always has.

evening: The day isn't finished. Neither are you.
Evening. You have tasks left. Focus.
Before you rest, complete what you began.
The night is quiet. Use it.
Hmph. Still something left. Do it now.
Don't let the day end on a loose thread.
game: Sit. Close your eyes if you want. Follow the light.
Thoughts will come. Let them pass. Return to the breath.
Slower. You're not in a race.
Good. The mind is a muscle too.
Don't judge the breath. Just notice it.
Stillness is a technique. You're learning it.
Your shoulders are up. Drop them.
Nothing else needs you right now.
game_done: Done. You're calmer. Don't waste it.
Carry that quiet into the rest of the day.
Good. Now go and do one thing well.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A waterfall thunders into a deep pool. Piccolo sits on a rock beneath it, the water pouring over his shoulders. He does not open his eyes.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Sit.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Under the waterfall?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Next to it. You'd drown under it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You sit on the wet rock beside him. The noise is enormous. Spray soaks you in seconds.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: For how long?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Until you stop asking.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Your mind races. The cold. The noise. Dinner. A conversation from last week you should have handled better.

choice.text: Try to block out the noise.

then.speaker: NARRATOR
then.text: You push against the noise. It pushes back harder. After ten minutes you have a headache.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: You're fighting it. You'll lose. The waterfall has been here longer than you.

then.speaker: NARRATOR
then.text: You stop pushing. The noise is still there, but it's just noise now. A thing that's happening.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Hm. Better.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Noise isn't the enemy. Attention that runs after the noise is the enemy.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Let it roar. Stay where you are.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: An hour passes. Maybe two. When he finally stands, you realise you haven't thought about dinner in a long time.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Again tomorrow.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Put these on. Cape and all.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He hands you a turban and a cape. The turban alone weighs more than your bag. The cape drags you sideways.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: They weigh a ton. How do you think in these?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: That's the point. Learn to focus while something drags at you.

choice.text: Why not focus without them first?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Because you'll never be without them. Not really. There's always something dragging at you. Tiredness, worry, someone else's opinion.

choice.text: Okay. What do I focus on?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Your breath. Only that. The weight will try to take your attention. Don't let it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You stand in the wasteland wearing his clothes, trying to breathe slowly while your shoulders scream.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You're thinking about the weight.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: It's hard not to.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Then think about it once, deliberately. Notice it. Say 'heavy'. Then go back to your breath.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You try it. 'Heavy.' Back to breath. 'Heavy.' Back to breath. It gets slightly easier.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Something always will drag at you. The weight is just honest about it.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Wear them every morning for a week. Then we'll talk.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: How do I stop getting distracted?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You don't.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Then what's the point of all this?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You get distracted. You notice. You return. A thousand times a day.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: The returning is the exercise. Stop treating it as failure.

choice.text: But I want to stay focused.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: You want to never fall over. Nobody walks like that. They fall a little and catch themselves, every step.

choice.text: So every time I get distracted is practice?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Yes. Every time you notice and come back. That's one repetition.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: People think good focus means never drifting. It doesn't. It means drifting less far, and coming back sooner.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: How do I come back sooner?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: By practising coming back. There's no other way. It's a muscle like any other.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: When you meditate and your mind wanders a hundred times, you didn't fail a hundred times. You trained a hundred times.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You think about that for a while. It feels like something heavy being put down.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Now sit. Count your breaths to ten. When you lose count, start again. Don't be angry about it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Piccolo raises two fingers to his forehead and holds them there. Minutes pass.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Nothing's happening.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Everything is happening. I'm gathering it to one point.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A faint crackle of light begins at his fingertips. It grows, very slowly.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Scattered effort scratches. Gathered effort pierces.

choice.text: How long does it take to gather?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Longer than people like. That's why most people never do it. They fire off half-ready and wonder why it didn't work.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Not the technique. Not yet. The principle, yes. Today.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Look at your days. How many things are you doing at once?

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: A lot.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: And how many of them go deep?

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: ...Not many.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Pick one thing a day to do completely. Phone away. Door shut. One thing, all the way through. That's one point.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He lowers his hand. The light fades.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: The next time you fight, I'll stand with you.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A storm breaks over the wasteland. Rain comes sideways. Lightning hits the cliff close enough to feel. Piccolo does not move.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Shouldn't we take shelter?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Can you hold your mind still out here?

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then an hour of your work is worth more than an hour of anyone else's. Stay.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Then this is the hour to find out. Stay.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You stay. You're soaked. Every crack of thunder makes your heart jump.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Notice the jump. Don't follow it. Let the heart settle on its own.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The next crack comes. Your heart jumps. You notice, and breathe. It settles faster than before.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Calm on a quiet day is nothing. Anyone is calm in a quiet room.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Calm in a storm is training. It's the only kind that counts when something goes wrong.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The storm passes after an hour. The sky is suddenly, ridiculously blue.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: I did it.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You did it once. Now do it on a bad day at work, in a traffic jam, in an argument. Those are the real storms.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It's late. Piccolo is looking at something far away that you can't see.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I trained a child once. Small. Cried constantly.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: What happened to him?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: He stopped crying. Then he became stronger than me.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: ...I don't use that word.

then.speaker: NARRATOR
then.text: His ears twitch. He doesn't say anything else for a moment.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Badly, at first. I left him alone in the wild. I thought hardness was the only lesson.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: I was harder on him than he deserved. I won't apologise. But I remember.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: He forgave me before I understood what I'd done. That's who he was. Who he still is.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Do you still see him?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: When he has time. He studies now. Books. Exams. He trains less than he should.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: He told me once that the meditation helps him study. Not fight. Study.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Something in his voice is almost soft.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: That's what training is for. It was never about fighting. Remember that, when you forget why you do it.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You sit together on the cliff edge for an hour. Neither of you speaks.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The wind moves. A hawk circles below you. The sun shifts from one rock to the next.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You notice your mind wander. You bring it back. It wanders less far this time.

then.speaker: NARRATOR
then.text: You stay silent. It's not hard today. It's almost easy.

then.speaker: NARRATOR
then.text: You glance over. His eyes are closed. Somehow, he seems to know you looked, and doesn't mind.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Another half hour. Your legs are stiff. You don't move them.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Hm.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You didn't fidget. First time.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Is that good?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: It means your body has stopped needing to escape. It's the start of real stillness.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Most people never get here. They fill every quiet moment with noise because quiet frightens them.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He stands, slowly, and looks at the horizon.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Same time tomorrow. Bring nothing.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: I've seen you lose an arm and grow it back. Does it hurt?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He doesn't elaborate. You wait. Eventually, he does.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: It takes energy and it takes focus. Panic makes it slower. If you panic, the energy goes everywhere at once.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: But what's lost comes back, if you don't panic.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: It's useful to you too, though you can't regrow anything.

choice.text: I wish I could do that.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: You can. Not with arms. With everything else.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Your bad days work the same way. You recover faster now. I've been watching.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: I still have bad days.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Of course. But a month ago, one bad day became three. Now one bad day is one bad day. Then you come back.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: That's regrowth. You lost something, and you didn't panic, and it came back.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He flexes his hand, the one that was once gone.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Remember this the next time you break a streak. It's an arm. It grows back.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The usual cliff. The usual silence. Then, unusually, Piccolo speaks first.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: Stand up.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Is the session over?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: The lessons are. You have a quiet mind. I can't improve on it.

choice.text: There must be more to learn.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: There's always more. But you don't need a teacher for it any more. You need time.

then.speaker: PICCOLO
then.text: Don't. You did the sitting. I just stood nearby looking disapproving.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: When you first came, you sat down like you were waiting for a bus. Now you sit like you live here.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Can I still come back?

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: The cliff isn't mine. Sit on it whenever you like.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: ...And if you come at dawn, I'll probably be here. Not that it matters.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You understand that this is an invitation. Possibly the warmest one he's ever given.

lines.speaker: PICCOLO
lines.text: You did well. I won't say it twice.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He turns back to the horizon. After a moment, you sit down beside him. Neither of you speaks. It's the best conversation you've had all week.
